title: Fujifilm is raising camera prices by up to €500. The AI memory crisis has reached photography.

content_html:
TL;DR

Fujifilm is raising prices on five cameras from September 1 due to the DRAM crisis. X100 VI up €200, GFX100 II up €500. The memory shortage that hit smartphones and laptops has reached cameras.

Fujifilm is raising list prices on at least five camera models from September 1, blaming the global DRAM crisis for rising production costs. The X100 VI climbs €200 to €1,999 ($2,119). The X-E5, X-T50, and X-S20 each go up €100. The steepest hike lands on the medium-format GFX100 II, which jumps €500 to €8,499, putting it €1,000 above its direct rival, Hasselblad’s X2D II.

This is not a Fujifilm problem. It is the same memory shortage that has been working through every electronics category since AI data centres began absorbing the world’s DRAM supply. The AI boom is killing the cheap smartphone because memory makers redirected wafer capacity to high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators, leaving less for the LPDDR and DDR chips that go into phones, laptops, and cameras. Budget smartphones under $100 have become nearly impossible to manufacture profitably. Samsung raised prices across its entire foldable lineup by $100 per model. Qualcomm is raising chip prices by double digits. TSMC is expected to hike manufacturing costs roughly 10%.

Camera sensors and image processors depend on the same DRAM and NAND supply chain. Fujifilm estimates the memory crisis will cost it around ¥11 billion in 2026. Canon and Fujifilm told investors they have secured most of the memory needed for this year, which may delay further increases, but with RAM prices projected to climb another 40-50% this quarter, the pressure is not easing. Apple raised iPhone 17 prices 10% in Japan due to currency and component pressure, and camera manufacturers face the same headwinds with smaller margins to absorb them.

Canon, Sony, and Nikon have not announced increases yet, but they buy from the same suppliers and face the same cost structure. The DRAM crisis does not discriminate by product category. It hits everything with a processor and memory inside it, from phones to laptops to cars to cameras. The difference is that camera buyers tend to notice a €500 price hike more than a smartphone buyer notices €50, because a GFX100 II is a considered purchase, not an impulse one. Fujifilm is the first to move. The rest will follow.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

由于 DRAM 危机，富士胶片从 9 月 1 日起提高了五款相机的价格。 X100 VI 上涨 200 欧元，GFX100 II 上涨 500 欧元。 智能手机和笔记本电脑的内存短缺已经影响到了相机。

富士胶片将从 9 月 1 日起提高至少五款相机型号的标价，并将生产成本上涨归咎于全球 DRAM 危机。 X100 VI 价格上涨 200 欧元，至 1,999 欧元（2,119 美元）。 X-E5、X-T50 和 X-S20 各上涨 100 欧元。 涨幅最大的是中画幅 GFX100 II，其价格上涨了 500 欧元，达到 8,499 欧元，比其直接竞争对手哈苏的 X2D II 高出 1,000 欧元。

这不是富士胶片的问题。 自人工智能数据中心开始吸收全球 DRAM 供应以来，每个电子类别都存在同样的内存短缺问题。 人工智能热潮正在扼杀廉价智能手机，因为内存制造商将晶圆产能转向用于人工智能加速器的高带宽内存，留给手机、笔记本电脑和相机的 LPDDR 和 DDR 芯片的产能减少。 100 美元以下的廉价智能手机几乎不可能实现盈利。 三星将其整个可折叠产品线的每个型号的价格提高了 100 美元。 高通正在将芯片价格提高两位数。 台积电预计将制造成本上调约 10%。

相机传感器和图像处理器依赖于相同的 DRAM 和 NAND 供应链。 富士胶片估计，到 2026 年，内存危机将使其损失约 110 亿日元。 佳能和富士胶片告诉投资者，他们已经获得了今年所需的大部分内存，这可能会推迟进一步的涨价，但由于 RAM 价格预计本季度将再上涨 40-50%，压力并未缓解。 由于汇率和零部件压力，苹果将 iPhone 17 在日本的价格提高了 10%，而相机制造商也面临着同样的阻力，但其利润却较小。

佳能、索尼和尼康尚未宣布涨价，但它们从相同的供应商处采购，并面临相同的成本结构。 DRAM 危机不分产品类别。 它可以覆盖所有内置处理器和内存的东西，从手机到笔记本电脑，从汽车到相机。 不同之处在于，相机购买者更容易注意到 500 欧元的价格上涨，而不是智能手机购买者注意到的 50 欧元，因为 GFX100 II 是经过深思熟虑的购买，而不是冲动购买。 富士胶片率先行动。 其余的将随之而来。
